title: Set up a build pipeline for a repository
summary: Add the shared build workflow to your repository so that every pull request is built, tested and scanned, and every merge produces a signed release image.

resources.title: Shared workflows
resources.description: Build, test, scan and sign workflows for Go, Java, Node and Python.

resources.title: Skill: add the build pipeline
resources.description: Detects the language of your repository and adds the right workflow file.

prerequisites.title: A repository on GitHub
prerequisites.description: You need admin rights on it to add the deploy secret and branch protection.

prerequisites.title: Project in SonarQube
prerequisites.description: Created automatically for new repositories; check it exists under the repository name.

actors.name: You
actors.description: An engineer of the team that owns the repository.

steps.title: Add the shared workflow file
instructions: Copy the example for your language from the shared-workflows README.
Set the service id and the image name.

steps.title: Connect the pipeline to Secret Manager
steps.description: The pipeline reads the deploy secret from Secret Manager through workload identity. No secret is stored in GitHub.
instructions: In repository settings, add the variable GCP_PROJECT with your project id.
Run 'make pipeline-identity' from the shared-workflows repository with your repository name.
Check that no secret value was added under Settings › Secrets.

steps.title: Build, test and scan the pull request
steps.description: The workflow builds the code, runs the unit tests, runs SonarQube and the dependency scan, and builds an image.

steps.title: Ask Developer Experience for help
steps.description: Post the link to the failed run in #devex. Most failures are a missing test command or a wrong image name.

steps.title: Require the checks before merging
instructions: Turn on 'Require status checks to pass' and select build, test and sonarqube.
Turn on 'Require a pull request before merging' with one approval.

steps.title: Check a signed release image is produced
instructions: Open the artifact registry of your project and find the new image.
Check that the image has a signature next to its version.
steps.outcome: A signed image for every merge
